c.tagline: Réunion's Créole capital on the Barachois seafront, a French-Indian Ocean gateway to the Piton de la Fournaise volcano and the island's soaring cirques.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis are available but relatively pricey; confirm the fare for longer trips. No major ride-hailing apps operate on Réunion. The urban Citalis buses and island-wide Car Jaune coaches are the budget option, but most visitors rent a car to reach the volcano and cirques.

emergency.note: Réunion is a French department with full French emergency services: 112 is the EU-wide number, 17 is the police and 15 is the SAMU medical service.

avoid.reason: The Le Chaudron district on the eastern edge has a reputation for unrest and petty crime and is best avoided at night.
Car break-ins are the main issue — leave nothing visible in rentals, and the city centre gets very quiet after dark.

hood_desc: The palm-lined seafront promenade with its row of old colonial cannons, food trucks and weekend strollers facing the Indian Ocean; the city's social heart and the best place for a sunset walk, a run or a café stop.

The historic core along Rue de Paris and Avenue de la Victoire, lined with restored Créole mansions, the cathedral, the Léon Dierx fine-arts museum, the Natural History Museum and the main shops; the walkable base for first-timers.

A large, modern district holding the university campus of Le Moufia, big shopping centres, the Papang cable-car terminus and the Chaudron neighbourhood; busy, local and the closest quarter to Roland Garros airport.
A residential hillside just above the centre with hospitals, embassy-style villas and cooler air; leafy and calmer, with sweeping views back over the city and out to sea.
A quiet residential hillside reached by a winding cliff road west of the city, offering panoramic ocean views, cooler temperatures and a green, laid-back pace away from the downtown bustle.
lodging: Best Western Plus La Villa Saint-Denis

water.note: Tap water is safe in the main towns, though boil-water notices can follow cyclones.

transit.pay: Citalis urban buses and the Papang cable car take cash or a rechargeable card; a single Citalis ride is about €1.60. Car Jaune interurban coaches to the rest of the island are paid by cash or card, with fares by distance (roughly €2-8).
transit.hours: Citalis buses run roughly 5:00 AM to 8:00 PM with limited evening service; the Papang aerial cable car links Bois-de-Nèfles and Le Chaudron. Taxis or a rental car fill the late-night gaps.
transit.note: Saint-Denis has no metro or passenger rail (the old colonial railway closed in the 1970s). The urban Citalis bus network covers the city, the island-wide Car Jaune coaches connect to other towns, and the Papang aerial cable car (opened 2022) serves the eastern heights; most visitors still rent a car to reach the volcano and cirques.

car.idp: Not required for EU licenses; an IDP is recommended for other nationalities

transit.m: Car Jaune 'Zéclair' express bus to Saint-Denis centre (~20-30 min)
Taxi to the city centre (15-20 min)

tip.r: Service is included by law ('service compris'); tipping is not expected, though rounding up or leaving a few euros for good service is appreciated.
